caption:
Digitalization and #AI are reshaping the clean energy transition, raising critical questions about skills, inclusion, and opportunity.

At the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) Assembly, I joined a series of sessions exploring how digitalization and AI can strengthen integrity and efficiency, empower youth, and shape the future of renewable energy jobs. I just wanted to re-share my three reflections: 

1️⃣ Innovation in #energy is not new
While digital and AI tools are accelerating change, innovation has long driven progress in the energy sector. We have fantastic innovation talent and heritage within and across the sector - and huge opportunities to amplify this. We need to explore and embrace new tech and new opportunities, but also build on our existing learning too. 

2️⃣ A broad and future-ready talent pipeline is essential
'#Digital', 'AI', and 'energy' are not discrete or homogenous jobs or sectors. They are wide-ranging and interlinked - and even inter-disciplinary. So, when we're talking about shaping the jobs of the future, we need to think broadly. There isn't a single 'energy' job, but a whole pipeline of different opportunities and entry-points. 

3️⃣ Energy talent is everywhere
All voices need to be represented and participate in energy policy, design, and delivery. Women are still under-represented in the sector, whilst the Global South is home to phenomenal talent building and deploying energy systems and solutions. We need to empower, platform, champion, and support this next generation of energy talent - wherever it's found.


#IRENA16A #EnergyForDevelopment
